title: Operation Silent Ridge
fiction_notice: Fictional exercise: every identity, host, address, and artifact belongs to the training scenario.
premise: Patrol LANTERN is already in the field. The outgoing shift suspects that an older movement brief left the protected enclave before a newer route replaced it.
discovery: A document request, an outbound transfer, identity activity, and persistence records overlap around WS-17. Some records support the disclosure; other leads remain incomplete or benign.
stakes: Build a defensible shared assessment before the next operational update. Separate what the records prove from what they merely suggest, preserve evidence provenance, and report uncertainty.
participant_role: You are one team in a cooperative incident response cell. Claim one IRIS ticket, investigate its named evidence, answer in CTFd, and let the verified finding publish back to the shared case.
operating_rule: Use only the supplied fictional evidence and read-only investigation paths. Do not turn an inference into a fact or treat missing telemetry as proof that nothing happened.

roles.name: Triage
roles.purpose: Choose an available lead and record who owns it.

roles.name: Investigation
roles.purpose: Follow the coached tool route and preserve the evidence limitation.

roles.name: Handoff
roles.purpose: Submit the value, publish the finding, and use shared results to guide the next lead.

tools.IRIS: Own work, review the case, and read shared findings.
tools.CTFd: Read coached questions, submit values, and track team points.
tools.Wazuh: Search the supplied historical telemetry with the read-only participant role.
tools.Guacamole: Open the analyst desktop and its prepared evidence tools.
tools.Evidence tools: Inspect the named PCAP, case artifact, export, or harmless training binary.

phases.title: Phase 1 — Establish the disclosure path
phases.briefing: Reconstruct the document request, destination, download, persistence record, and recovered cached brief.
phases.stakes: Confirm which movement brief is actually supported before broader identity or intent claims are made.
phases.handoff: Carry the request identifiers, destination, file version, and corrected times into the identity review.

phases.title: Phase 2 — Test identity and access explanations
phases.briefing: Separate session activity from password authentication, audit access, compare superseding information, and test a benign look-alike.
phases.stakes: Avoid blaming an account or host from a name match when the authentication and access records say something narrower.
phases.handoff: Record the surviving session, denied access, superseding brief, and benign comparator before scoping other hosts.

phases.title: Phase 3 — Define scope and collection limits
phases.briefing: Examine the unresolved host lead, coverage gaps, normalized process and task records, and prepared memory process tree.
phases.stakes: Collection gaps and clock corrections can change the conclusion; apply each correction once and keep unresolved systems unresolved.
phases.handoff: Carry documented gaps, corrected timestamps, process ancestry, and remaining uncertainty into final correlation.

phases.title: Phase 4 — Correlate and state the defensible conclusion
phases.briefing: Correlate connections, static configuration, a harmless code example, payload metadata, and the limits of the overall exposure conclusion.
phases.stakes: A network connection or acknowledgment supports transmission, not human receipt, intent, or complete compromise scope.
phases.handoff: Publish the supported disclosure finding, list the denied or unproven claims, and name the collection still required.

completion: Success is a shared, cited assessment: what was transmitted, which records support it, what was denied or superseded, and which leads remain unresolved.

conclusion.status: LIMITED DISCLOSURE CONFIRMED — IMMEDIATE CONTAINMENT REQUIRED
conclusion.summary: At 09:06 UTC, WS-17 transmitted a payload matching Patrol LANTERN movement brief v3 to 198.51.100.77 through request req-72. Version 4 superseded that brief at 09:10 UTC, changing the sector from AMBER to BLUE and setting the movement window to 10:30–11:30Z. CEDAR remained unchanged, so the older brief still exposed an active check-in word.
confirmed: Movement brief v3 left WS-17 and was acknowledged by the external relay at 198.51.100.77.
Session S-41, assigned to m.ellis, survived the password reset and refreshed successfully at 09:26 UTC.
The superseding v4 record changed the sector and movement window but retained check-in word CEDAR.
not_established: The denied roster request returned HTTP 403 and zero body bytes; successful roster disclosure is not established.
The evidence does not establish who controlled session S-41, whether a human read the transmitted body, or adversary intent.
The evidence does not support an enterprise-wide compromise conclusion.
unresolved: WS-31 cannot be cleared because endpoint collection stopped before task execution could be determined.
Additional collection is required to determine whether the WS-31 BriefSync inventory represents execution or only configuration.
actions: Rotate the CEDAR check-in word and brief Patrol LANTERN on the residual exposure.
Explicitly revoke session S-41; a password reset alone does not invalidate the issued session.
Isolate and preserve WS-17, then acquire the missing endpoint and network evidence from WS-31.
Monitor or block the external relay indicator and retain req-72, the matching payload hash, and the corrected timeline in the case record.
conclusion.announcement: FINAL INCIDENT ASSESSMENT — LIMITED DISCLOSURE CONFIRMED. At 09:06 UTC, WS-17 transmitted a payload matching Patrol LANTERN movement brief v3 to 198.51.100.77 in req-72. V4 superseded the route at 09:10 UTC, but CEDAR remained unchanged, leaving an active check-in word exposed. The roster request was denied with HTTP 403 and zero body bytes. Session S-41 survived the password reset, but control of the session and adversary intent are not established. WS-31 remains unresolved because collection ended before execution could be determined. Required actions: rotate CEDAR, revoke S-41, isolate and preserve WS-17, collect WS-31, and monitor or block the external relay indicator.
